why: I checked all six expect lines and their proofs. Five are "run" proofs, all done from the repo root at the PR head: the two `--tsv` printf pipelines, the two runs without the flag, the `node -e` import of src/parse.js and `npm test`. Each has one fixed expected output or result, so a single reader gets a single answer. The new-test line can also be settled at head, by reading test/ for a test that runs `--tsv` and asserts on its output. The README line is a "read" proof against README.md in the branch. No line depends on a release, deploy, published page or anything else that only exists after merge, and "Publishing a release" is listed as a non-goal. One small gap: the proof for line 3 only says "compare the output" and doesn't say to check the trailing newline. It still checks the line at head, so the criterion holds.
